newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Britain working on draft to condemn Iraqi actions.
newsitem.headline: Britain working on draft to condemn Iraqi actions.

text.p: Britain is working on a Security Council resolution that would condemn Iraq's weekend attack on Kurds in the north of the country and call for a return to the status quo, diplomats said Tuesday.
They said the aim was to draw on elements shared by all or most council members and come up with a consensus draft.
"Saddam Hussein is testing international opinion and international opinion should respond," one Western source said.

The draft, still the subject of negotiations, would recall council resolution 688 of 1991, which condemned the repression of Iraqi civilians, including Kurds, after Saddam Hussein's defeat in the Gulf war, and condemn the recent attacks on Kurds as a new element of instability in the region.
The resolution was also likely to express concern that Iraq's action threatened efforts to provide humanitarian aid for its civilian population under an "oil-for-food" plan.

The plan, agreed between Iraq and the United Nations in May on the basis of an April 1995 council resolution, had been expected to go into effect later this month. But on Sunday Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali announced a delay because the current fighting prevented the deployment in northern Iraq of U.N. inspectors to monitor the scheme.
The proposed British draft was also expected to express concern for the safety of U.N. and civilian staff involved in aid projects in northern Iraq.
It seemed unlikley that sufficient support could be mustered to endorse the missile strikes carried out by the United States in response to Baghdad's attack on Arbil and other Kurdish areas.
